mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.00% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.00% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 9.5% is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak labor market conditions prompt market participants to anticipate lower wage growth and slower economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 9.5% in a month
regime_hint: Elevated unemployment and slowing wage growth
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggers, the average 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (mean < 0 with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% in the same month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The interaction coefficient in a two-variable regression is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or the IC is below 0.05 over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% for two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥ 8% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 5 such contraction periods, the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (mean ≥ 0 with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00% for three consecutive months, the persistence of ultra-loose policy is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets price in accommodative conditions.
failure_condition: Across 10 such episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (mean ≤ 0 with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2,000K accompanied by a simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 10% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to recessionary expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls ≥ 2,000K and UNRATE rises above 10% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market stress and rising unemployment
failure_condition: The interaction term in a regression is not significant (p > 0.05) or the IC is above 0.10 over a 12-month post-trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (housing starts) exceeding 1,200K while CPIAUCSL is flat or declining suggests a demand-driven housing cycle, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (mean ≤ 0 with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month and INDPRO is flat, it indicates weak consumer spending and supply-side constraints, which precede a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls ≥ 10% and INDPRO is unchanged in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction coefficient in a regression is not significant (p > 0.05) or the IC is above 0.10 over a 6-month post-trigger window.
